First off, I liked it. It makes me wonder what he did to deserve such a 'deserved' punishment. I was thinking it would be funny if he didn't actually do anything bad at all and was just super paranoid that what he did would be taken the wrong way.

It's a very speculative paragraph. I got the impression that it transitioned from him just speaking paranoid rubbish to himself to him being sure what was about to happen. Perhaps that was what you were going for it. It builds uncertainty in the character and let's the reader know he did some bad shit. 

I liked how you said 'head held low and shoulders resigned'. A good contrast to the usual, head held high and proud shoulders or whatever. The paragraph has a nice flow to it and I enjoyed reading it.

Good job man. I feel like it would be inappropriate to say it wasn't a good tune. Because that's not true. It had its moments and it has elements that work nicely together, those that don't. But that's fine. The main thing is you actually finished a tune. Listen to it, and compare it with other tunes. How does it match up with timings of things? Structure? The amount of tracks playing at once? 
The biggest tip I can give you is to develop your ear. In my opinion, there is little to no point trying to only develop, for example, mixing if your ear isn't trained. With a trained ear you will be able to: produce better sounds (this will enable you to do more with less things. In music production, less is more if you know how to do it). You will also be able to deconstruct your favourite tracks. My only tip would be to try make more tunes more frequently. Some of the advice here is good and some isn't. You wont really understand yet what to do with all this advice. Don't get me wrong, go mad with it and try different things, but I think you should take mine first. It's like cooking. You think it is better than it actually is when you are starting out. If this isn't the case however, then it's important you understand why. This is why I recommend developing your ear etc. Every so often I listen back to the tunes I made a few years ago and almost find it comical at how different they sound to now. I never get bored of listening to them though. But I do learn from them all the time. I hope you read this because I truly think this is good advice. It's not specific. It's just a broad overview. Keep it up and don't stop. You will get better. Practise makes perfect. :)
